<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000474_dcnt_6ef8a3c0-65fc-4e12-8452-ebc98b22f8c4" continuedAt="F_000474_dcnt_ecb43947-3c8d-4a43-8c43-834995cb0019"><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000529" name="cit:PrepaidRailcarCertificationCostsPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001171825_20190101_20191231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Prepaid Railcar Certification Costs</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company incurs certain costs related to rail tank car safety certifications. These certification costs provide a long-term benefit to the Company as they allow the rail tank cars to comply with government standards and, as such, secure the use of these assets over future periods. These costs are accounted for as a prepaid expense, are classified within Other Assets and are amortized over the life cycle of the anticipated benefit of the re-certification (approximately <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000662" name="us-gaap:FiniteLivedIntangibleAssetUsefulLife" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapFiniteLivedIntangibleAssetsByMajorClassAxis_citPrepaidRailcarCertificationCostsMember_20190101_20191231" format="ixt-sec:duryear">10</ix:nonNumeric> years).</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000530" name="us-gaap:CompensationRelatedCostsPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001171825_20190101_20191231" escape="true">
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Stock-Based Compensation</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Compensation expense associated with equity-based awards is recognized over the vesting period (requisite service period), which is generally <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000663" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingPeriod1" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapPerformanceSharesMember_20190101_20191231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">three years</ix:nonNumeric>, under the &#8220;graded vesting&#8221; attribution method, whereby each vesting tranche of the award is amortized separately as if each were a separate award. The cost of awards granted to directors in lieu of cash is recognized using the single grant approach with immediate vesting and expense recognition. Expenses related to stock-based compensation are included in operating expenses (compensation and benefits).</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000531" name="us-gaap:LifeInsuranceCorporateOrBankOwnedTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001171825_20190101_20191231" escape="true">
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Bank-Owned Life Insurance</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">CIT purchased life insurance policies on the lives of certain officers and employees and is the owner and beneficiary of the policies. These policies, known as BOLI, offset the cost of providing employee benefits. CIT records these BOLI policies as a separate line item in the Consolidated Balance Sheets at each policy&#8217;s respective cash surrender value, with changes recorded as other non-interest income in the Consolidated Statements of Income.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000532" name="us-gaap:EarningsPerSharePolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001171825_20190101_20191231" escape="true">
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Earnings per Share (&#8220;EPS&#8221;)</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Basic EPS is computed by dividing net income available to common shareholders by the weighted-average number of common shares outstanding for the period. Diluted EPS is computed by dividing net income available to common shareholders by the weighted-average number of common shares outstanding increased by the weighted-average potential impact of dilutive securities. The Company's potential dilutive instruments primarily include restricted unvested stock grants and performance stock grants. The dilutive effect is computed using the treasury stock method, which assumes the conversion of these instruments. However, in periods when there is a net loss, these shares would not be included in the EPS computation as the result would have an anti-dilutive effect.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000533" name="cit:TreasuryStockRetirementPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001171825_20190101_20191231" escape="true">
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Treasury Stock Retirement </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company may choose to retire treasury shares that it acquires through share repurchases and return those shares to the status of authorized but unissued. The Company accounts for treasury stock transactions under the cost method. For each reacquisition of common stock, the number of shares and the acquisition price for those shares is added to the existing treasury stock count and total value. When treasury shares are retired, the Company's policy is to allocate the excess of the repurchase price over the par value of shares acquired to both retained earnings and paid-in capital. The portion allocated to paid-in capital is determined by applying a percentage, which is determined by dividing the number of shares to be retired by the number of shares issued, to the balance of additional paid-in capital as of the retirement date.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000534" name="us-gaap:CostsAssociatedWithExitOrDisposalActivitiesOrRestructuringsPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001171825_20190101_20191231" escape="true">
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Accounting for Costs Associated with Exit or Disposal Activities</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">A liability for costs associated with exit or disposal activities, other than in a business combination, is recognized when the liability is incurred. The liability is measured at fair value, with adjustments for changes in estimated cash flows recognized in earnings.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000535" name="cit:ConsolidatedStatementsOfCashFlowsPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001171825_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000535_dcnt_951bdc29-a8c3-4523-8d7b-71bdce8ae822">
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Unrestricted cash and cash equivalents includes cash and interest-bearing deposits, which are primarily overnight money market investments and short term investments in mutual funds. The Company maintains cash balances principally at financial institutions located in the U.S. The balances are not insured in all cases. Cash and cash equivalents also include amounts at CIT Bank, which are only available for the bank&#8217;s funding and investment requirements. Cash inflows and outflows from customer deposits are presented on a net basis. Factoring receivables are presented on a net basis, as a part of change in loans, in the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, as factoring receivables are generally due in less than 90 days.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cash receipts and cash payments resulting from purchases and sales of loans, securities, and other financing and leasing assets are classified as operating cash flows when these assets are originated/acquired and designated specifically for sale.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Activity for loans originated or acquired for investment purposes, including those subsequently transferred to AHFS, is classified in the investing section of the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows.&#160;&#160;The vast majority of the Company&#8217;s loan originations are for investment purposes. Cash receipts resulting from sales of loans, beneficial interests and other loans and leases that were not specifically originated and/or acquired and designated for resale are classified as investing cash inflows regardless of subsequent classification.</p></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">109</p>
<p style="text-align:right;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">CIT ANNUAL REPORT 2019</p>

<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000474_dcnt_ecb43947-3c8d-4a43-8c43-834995cb0019" continuedAt="F_000474_dcnt_636b7741-d6af-41ed-bc0e-5e9f82071b3f"><ix:continuation id="F_000535_dcnt_951bdc29-a8c3-4523-8d7b-71bdce8ae822">
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The cash flows related to investment securities and loans (excluding loans held for sale) purchased at a premium or discount are as follows:</span></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Restricted cash includes cash on deposit with other banks that are legally restricted as to withdrawal and primarily serve as collateral for certain servicer obligations of the Company. At December 31, 2019, restricted cash included amounts set aside in escrow related to the acquisition of MOB. CIT presents restricted cash activity within the net change in cash and cash equivalents and as part of the beginning and ending balances of cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash in the Statements of Cash Flows, along with a reconciliation of those balances in the Statements of Cash Flows to those shown on the Balance Sheet. See <span style="font-style:italic;">Note 29 &#8211; Subsequent Events.</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Activity of discontinued operations is included in various line items of the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows and summary items are disclosed in <span style="font-style:italic;">Note 2 &#8211; Discontinued Operations</span>.</p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000536" name="cit:AccountingPronouncementsAdoptedPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001171825_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000536_dcnt_14620cf5-5a79-4af9-914f-4a5df0384168">
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Accounting Pronouncements Adopted</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On January 1, 2019, the Company adopted the following Accounting Standards Updates (&#8220;ASU&#8221;) issued by the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#8220;FASB&#8221;):</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Leases and subsequent related ASUs</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ASU 2016-02, <span style="font-style:italic;">Leases (Topic 842),</span> and subsequent related ASUs modifies the accounting, presentation, and disclosures for both lessees and lessors. </p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">See further discussion in the <span style="font-style:italic;">Leases </span>Section<span style="font-style:italic;">.</span></p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Receivables - Nonrefundable Fees and Other Costs (Subtopic 310-20): Premium Amortization on Purchased Callable Debt Securities</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ASU 2017-08, <span style="font-style:italic;">Receivables - Nonrefundable Fees and Other Costs (Subtopic 310-20): Premium Amortization on Purchased Callable Debt Securities </span>shortens the amortization period for certain callable debt securities held at a premium. Specifically, the amendments require the premium to be amortized to the earliest call date.<span style="font-style:italic;"> </span>The new guidance applies to all entities that hold investments in callable debt securities for which the amortized cost basis exceeds the amount repayable by the issuer at the earliest call date (i.e., at a premium). </p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">CIT adopted this guidance as of January 1, 2019 using a modified retrospective transition approach. The adoption of this standard did not have a material impact on CIT&#8217;s consolidated financial statements and disclosures as unamortized premiums on debt securities are immaterial.</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Compensation - Stock Compensation (Topic 718): Improvements to Nonemployee Share-Base Payment Accounting</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ASU 2018-07, <span style="font-style:italic;">Compensation - Stock Compensation (Topic 718): Improvements to Nonemployee Share-Base Payment Accounting </span>supersedes ASC 505-50, <span style="font-style:italic;">Equity-Equity-Based Payments</span> <span style="font-style:italic;">to Non- Employees,</span> and expands the scope of ASC 718 to include all share-based payment arrangements related to the acquisition of goods and services from both nonemployees and employees. As a result, most of the guidance in ASC 718 associated with employee share-based payments, including most of its requirements related to classification and measurement, applies to nonemployee share-based payment arrangements. Entities should use a modified retrospective transition approach, with a cumulative-effect adjustment to retained earnings as of the beginning of the fiscal year, for all: (1) liability-classified nonemployee awards that have not been settled as of the adoption date and (2) equity-classified nonemployee awards for which a measurement date has not been established<span style="font-size:10pt;">.</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:2pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">CIT adopted this guidance as of January 1, 2019 using a modified retrospective transition approach. The adoption of this standard did not have a material impact on CIT&#8217;s consolidated financial statements and disclosures as CIT&#8217;s current accounting for nonemployee share-based payment is consistent with the requirements for employee share-based awards.</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Derivatives and Hedging (Topic 815): Inclusion of the Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) Overnight Index Swap (OIS) Rate as a Benchmark Interest Rate for Hedge Accounting Purposes</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ASU 2018-16,<span style="font-weight:bold;"> </span><span style="font-style:italic;">Derivatives and Hedging (Topic 815): Inclusion of the Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) Overnight Index Swap (OIS) Rate as a Benchmark Interest Rate for Hedge Accounting Purposes</span><span style="font-weight:bold;"> </span>permits the use of the OIS rate based on the SOFR as a U.S. benchmark interest rate for hedge accounting purposes under Topic 815 in addition to the United States Treasury (UST), the<span style="font-size:10pt;"> </span>London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR) swap rate, the OIS rate based on the Fed Funds Effective Rate, and the Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association (SIFMA) Municipal Swap Rate.<span style="font-weight:bold;"> </span>Including the OIS rate based on SOFR as an eligible benchmark interest rate during the early stages of the marketplace transition will facilitate the LIBOR to </p></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">110</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">CIT ANNUAL REPORT 2019</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000474_dcnt_636b7741-d6af-41ed-bc0e-5e9f82071b3f" continuedAt="F_000474_dcnt_673e28d1-4389-4432-9283-86beb7b87553"><ix:continuation id="F_000536_dcnt_14620cf5-5a79-4af9-914f-4a5df0384168">
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">SOFR transition and provide sufficient lead time for entities to prepare for changes to interest rate risk hedging strategies for both risk management and hedge accounting purposes.</span><span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> Entities should adopt this guidance on a prospective basis for qualifying new or redesignated hedging relationships entered into on or after the date of adoption.</span></p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">CIT adopted this guidance as of January 1, 2019. The adoption of this standard did not have a material impact on CIT&#8217;s consolidated financial statements and disclosures as this amendment requires adoption on a prospective basis for qualifying new or redesignated hedging relationships entered into on or after the date of adoption.</p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000537" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001171825_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000537_dcnt_a276ce3b-ab14-4ac4-b4ae-54e039fd72b1">
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">RECENT ACCOUNTING PRONOUNCEMENTS</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:7pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The following accounting pronouncements have been issued by the FASB but are not yet effective as of December 31, 2019:</p>
<div>
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="margin:auto;border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="padding-left:3pt;padding-Right:2pt;width:20.7%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:2pt;margin-top:2pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Standard</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="padding-left:3pt;padding-Right:2pt;width:39.28%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:2pt;margin-top:2pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Summary of Guidance</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="padding-left:3pt;padding-Right:2pt;width:40.02%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:2pt;margin-top:2pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Effect on CIT's Financial Statements</p></td>
</tr></table></div></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">111</p>
<p style="text-align:right;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">CIT ANNUAL REPORT 2019</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000474_dcnt_673e28d1-4389-4432-9283-86beb7b87553" continuedAt="F_000474_dcnt_11d2c98b-5d71-4425-bd23-ae25db4f61e0"><ix:continuation id="F_000537_dcnt_a276ce3b-ab14-4ac4-b4ae-54e039fd72b1" continuedAt="F_000537_dcnt_653090fd-a99d-4f0b-bfb7-3f81927aabda">
<div>
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="margin:auto;border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="padding-left:3pt;padding-Right:2pt;width:20.7%; border-top:solid 2pt #000000; border-bottom:solid 2pt #000000;">
<p style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:2pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ASU 2016-13, <span style="font-style:italic;">Financial Instruments - Credit Losses (Topic 326): Measurement of Credit Losses on Financial Instruments, </span>and subsequent related ASUs</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:2pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:6pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Issued June 2016 with Updates through November 2019</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:6pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="padding-left:3pt;padding-Right:2pt;width:39.28%; border-top:solid 2pt #000000; border-bottom:solid 2pt #000000;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:27pt;;text-indent:-13.5pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;<span style="font-family:Arial;">ASU 2016-13 introduces a forward-looking &#8220;expected loss&#8221; model (the &#8220;Current Expected Credit Losses&#8221; (&#8220;CECL&#8221;) model) to estimate credit losses over the full remaining expected life of the portfolio upon adoption, rather than the incurred loss model under previous U.S. GAAP standards. Estimates of expected credit losses under the new model will be based on relevant information about past events, current conditions, and reasonable and supportable forecasts regarding the collectability of reported amounts. Generally, the new model requires that an allowance for credit losses (&#8220;ACL&#8221;) be estimated and recognized for financial assets measured at amortized cost within its scope.</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:27pt;;text-indent:-13.5pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;<span style="font-family:Arial;">The amendments in this standard eliminate existing guidance for Purchase Credit Impaired ("PCI") loans and require recognition of an allowance for expected credit losses on financial assets purchased with more than insignificant credit deterioration since origination (purchased credit deteriorated (&#8220;PCD&#8221;) loans).</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:27pt;;text-indent:-13.5pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;<span style="font-family:Arial;">Loans previously classified as PCI will be considered PCD at adoption, with a credit related discount reflected in the ACL and loan balance. </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:27pt;;text-indent:-13.5pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;<span style="font-family:Arial;">ASU 2016-13 amends existing impairment guidance for AFS securities to incorporate an allowance, which will allow for reversals of impairment losses if the credit of an issuer improves.</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:27pt;;text-indent:-13.5pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;<span style="font-family:Arial;">In addition, ASU 2016-13 expands the disclosure requirements regarding an entity&#8217;s assumptions, models, and methods for estimating the ACL.</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:27pt;;text-indent:-13.5pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;<span style="font-family:Arial;">ASU 2018-19 clarifies that receivables arising from operating leases are not within the scope of ASU 2016-13 and should be accounted for in accordance with Topic 842, </span><span style="font-style:italic;font-family:Arial;">Leases</span><span style="font-family:Arial;">. </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:27pt;;text-indent:-13.5pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;<span style="font-family:Arial;">ASU 2019-04 clarifies certain aspects of the credit losses standard and addresses issues related to accrued interest receivable balances, recoveries, as well as extension and renewal options, among other items. </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:27pt;;text-indent:-13.5pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;<span style="font-family:Arial;">ASU 2019-05 allows companies to </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:27pt;;;font-size:9pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-family:Arial;">irrevocably elect, upon adoption of ASU 2016-13, the fair value option on financial instruments that (1) were previously recorded at amortized cost and (2) are within the scope of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;">ASU 2016-13</span><span style="font-family:Arial;"> if the instruments are eligible for the fair value option under ASC 825-10. The fair value option election does not apply to held-to-maturity debt securities. </span><span style="font-family:Arial;">Entities are required to make this election on an instrument-by-instrument basis.</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:27pt;;text-indent:-13.5pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;<span style="font-family:Arial;">ASU 2019-11 permits entities to record a negative allowance when measuring the expected credit losses for a PCD financial asset, not to exceed the total amount of the amortized cost basis previously charged off and expected to be charged off. It allows entities to apply a similar approach when determining the ACL for PCD assets but does not permit the premature recognition of interest income.</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:27pt;;text-indent:-13.5pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;<span style="font-family:Arial;">Entities will apply the standard&#8217;s provisions as a cumulative-effect adjustment to retained earnings as of the beginning of the first reporting period in which the guidance is adopted (modified-retrospective approach).</span></p></td>
<td valign="top" style="padding-left:3pt;padding-Right:2pt;width:40.02%; border-top:solid 2pt #000000; border-bottom:solid 2pt #000000;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:30.75pt;;text-indent:-18pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;<span style="font-family:Arial;">CIT adopted this guidance as of January 1, 2020. </span></p>
<p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:30.75pt;;text-indent:-18pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;<span style="font-family:Arial;">CIT developed and implemented models and methodologies that are used to determine the CECL allowance. Key inputs into the models and methodologies include historical loss experience data, macroeconomic variable forecasts, position level data and management assumptions. CIT considers the macroeconomic forecasts used to be reasonable and supportable over the life of the loan portfolio. </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:30.75pt;;text-indent:-18pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;<span style="font-family:Arial;">As a result of the adoption, the ACL increases by approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000664" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableAllowanceForCreditLossesPeriodIncreaseDecrease" contextRef="C_0001171825_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_us-gaapAdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis_us-gaapAccountingStandardsUpdate201613Member_us-gaapSubsequentEventTypeAxis_us-gaapSubsequentEventMember_20200101_20200101" decimals="-6" scale="6">225</ix:nonFraction> - $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000665" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableAllowanceForCreditLossesPeriodIncreaseDecrease" contextRef="C_0001171825_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapAdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis_us-gaapAccountingStandardsUpdate201613Member_us-gaapSubsequentEventTypeAxis_us-gaapSubsequentEventMember_20200101_20200101" decimals="-6" scale="6">275</ix:nonFraction></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;"> </span><span style="font-family:Arial;">million effective January 1, 2020 (excluding the impact of the MOB acquisition completed on January 1, 2020). The presentation of a range for the January 1, 2020 adoption impact is included pending final model review, which may impact the reserve as of such date. </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:30.75pt;;text-indent:-18pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;<span style="font-family:Arial;">Approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000666" name="cit:IncreaseInPurchaseCreditImpairedLoansReclassifiedAsPurchasedCreditDeterioratedLoans" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapAdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis_us-gaapAccountingStandardsUpdate201613Member_20190101_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">120</ix:nonFraction> million of the increase is due to PCI loans that were reclassified as PCD loans with the credit related discount resulting in an increase to both the ACL and the loan balance. The reclassification from PCI to PCD does not&#59; however, result in an adoption date adjustment to retained earnings. </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:30.75pt;;text-indent:-18pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;<span style="font-family:Arial;">The remaining increase in ACL results in a decrease of approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000667" name="us-gaap:CumulativeEffectOnRetainedEarningsNetOfTax1" contextRef="C_0001171825_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_us-gaapAdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis_us-gaapAccountingStandardsUpdate201613Member_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_citMutualOfOmahaBankMember_us-gaapSubsequentEventTypeAxis_us-gaapSubsequentEventMember_20200101_20200101" decimals="-6" scale="6">75</ix:nonFraction> - $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000668" name="us-gaap:CumulativeEffectOnRetainedEarningsNetOfTax1" contextRef="C_0001171825_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapAdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis_us-gaapAccountingStandardsUpdate201613Member_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_citMutualOfOmahaBankMember_us-gaapSubsequentEventTypeAxis_us-gaapSubsequentEventMember_20200101_20200101" decimals="-6" scale="6">100</ix:nonFraction> million in retained earnings (after-tax) effective January 1, 2020 (excluding the impact of the MOB acquisition completed on January 1, 2020). Management plans to phase-in the transitional amounts impacting regulatory capital as follows: <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000669" name="cit:PercentageOfImpactInRegulatoryCapitalInFirstYearOfAdoption" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapAdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis_us-gaapAccountingStandardsUpdate201613Member_us-gaapSubsequentEventTypeAxis_us-gaapSubsequentEventMember_20200101_20200101" decimals="2" scale="-2">25</ix:nonFraction>% in the first year of adoption of CECL, <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000670" name="cit:PercentageOfImpactInRegulatoryCapitalInSecondYearOfAdoption" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapAdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis_us-gaapAccountingStandardsUpdate201613Member_us-gaapSubsequentEventTypeAxis_us-gaapSubsequentEventMember_20200101_20200101" decimals="2" scale="-2">50</ix:nonFraction>% in the second year, <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000671" name="cit:PercentageOfImpactInRegulatoryCapitalInThirdYearOfAdoption" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapAdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis_us-gaapAccountingStandardsUpdate201613Member_us-gaapSubsequentEventTypeAxis_us-gaapSubsequentEventMember_20200101_20200101" decimals="2" scale="-2">75</ix:nonFraction>% in the third year, with full impact beginning in the fourth year. Adoption of the new standard could produce higher volatility in the quarterly credit loss expense than the incurred loss model under current U.S. GAAP, depending on asset mix, forecast of future economic scenarios, or other factors, and could adversely impact our ongoing earnings.</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:30.75pt;;text-indent:-18pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;<span style="font-family:Arial;">For acquisitions subsequent to the adoption of CECL, CIT is required to record an allowance for non-PCD assets with a corresponding increase to the income statement Provision for credit losses. For acquired PCD loans, an allowance is required with a corresponding increase to the amortized cost basis as of the acquisition date. For PCD loans where all or a portion of the loan balance had been charged off prior to acquisition, for which active collection efforts are still underway, the CECL allowance included as part of the grossed-up loan balance at acquisition is immediately charged off. Additionally, CIT is required to consider its existing policies in determining whether to charge off any financial assets, regardless of whether a charge-off was recorded by the predecessor company.</span></p>
<p style="margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:36pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="padding-left:3pt;padding-Right:2pt;width:20.7%; border-top:solid 2pt #000000; border-bottom:solid 2pt #000000;">
<p style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:2pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ASU 2018-17, <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidation (Topic 810): Targeted Improvements to Related Party Guidance for Variable Interest Entities</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:2pt;margin-top:6pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Issued October 2018</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="padding-left:9pt;padding-Right:2pt;width:39.28%; border-top:solid 2pt #000000; border-bottom:solid 2pt #000000;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:21pt;;text-indent:-13.5pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;<span style="font-family:Arial;">The amendments in this guidance change how entities that apply the VIE guidance evaluate decision-making fees. To determine whether decision-making fees represent a variable interest, an entity will consider indirect interests held through related parties under common control on a proportional basis rather than in their entirety, as currently required by GAAP. </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:21pt;;text-indent:-13.5pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;<span style="font-family:Arial;">Entities should adopt this standard retrospectively with a cumulative-effect adjustment to retained earnings at the beginning of the earliest period presented.</span></p></td>
<td valign="top" style="padding-left:3pt;padding-Right:2pt;width:40.02%; border-top:solid 2pt #000000; border-bottom:solid 2pt #000000;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:30.75pt;;text-indent:-18pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;<span style="font-family:Arial;">CIT adopted this guidance as of January 1, 2020. </span></p>
<p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:30.75pt;;text-indent:-18pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;<span style="font-family:Arial;">The adoption of this standard did not have an impact on CIT&#8217;s consolidated financial statements and disclosures.</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:2pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:18pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="padding-left:3pt;padding-Right:2pt;width:20.7%; border-top:solid 2pt #000000; border-bottom:solid 2pt #000000;">
<p style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ASU 2019-04<span style="font-style:italic;">, Codification Improvements to Topic 326, Financial Instruments - Credit Losses, Topic 815, Derivatives and Hedging, and Topic 825, Financial Instruments </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:2pt;margin-top:6pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Issued April 2019</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="padding-left:3pt;padding-Right:2pt;width:39.28%; border-top:solid 2pt #000000; border-bottom:solid 2pt #000000;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:27pt;;text-indent:-13.5pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;<span style="font-family:Arial;">The FASB amended its standards on credit losses, hedging, and recognizing and measuring financial instruments to clarify them and address implementation issues. </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:27pt;;text-indent:-13.5pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;<span style="font-family:Arial;">Refer to ASU 2016-13 above for the amendments that clarify the scope of the credit losses standard. </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:27pt;;text-indent:-13.5pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;<span style="font-family:Arial;">With respect to codification improvements to Update 2017-12 and other hedge accounting, the amendments address partial-term fair value hedges, fair value hedge basis adjustments, and certain transition requirements, among other items.</span></p></td>
<td valign="top" style="padding-left:3pt;padding-Right:2pt;width:40.02%; border-top:solid 2pt #000000; border-bottom:solid 2pt #000000;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:30.75pt;;text-indent:-18pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;<span style="font-family:Arial;">CIT adopted this guidance as of January 1, 2020. </span></p>
<p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:30.75pt;;text-indent:-18pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;<span style="font-family:Arial;">The adoption of this standard did not have a material impact on CIT&#8217;s consolidated financial statements and disclosures.</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:2pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:18pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="padding-left:3pt;padding-Right:2pt;width:20.7%; border-top:solid 2pt #000000; border-bottom:solid 2pt #000000;">
<p style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ASU 2019-12, <span style="font-style:italic;">Income Taxes (Topic 740) Simplifying the Accounting for Income Taxes</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:2pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Issued November 2019</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="padding-left:3pt;padding-Right:2pt;width:39.28%; border-top:solid 2pt #000000; border-bottom:solid 2pt #000000;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:27pt;;text-indent:-13.5pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;<span style="font-family:Arial;">The amendments in this Update add new guidance to simplify accounting for income taxes, change the accounting for certain income tax transactions and make minor improvements to the codification. </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:27pt;;text-indent:-13.5pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;<span style="font-family:Arial;">The amendments in this Update have different transition requirements depending on the topic. </span></p></td>
<td valign="top" style="padding-left:3pt;padding-Right:2pt;width:40.02%; border-top:solid 2pt #000000; border-bottom:solid 2pt #000000;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:30.75pt;;text-indent:-18pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;<span style="font-family:Arial;">Effective for CIT as of January 1, 2021. Early adoption is permitted.</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:30.75pt;;text-indent:-18pt;;font-size:9pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;<span style="font-family:Arial;">CIT is currently evaluating the impact of this standard&#59; however, the Company does not expect the adoption of this guidance to have a material impact on its consolidated financial statements and disclosures.</span></p></td>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTE 2 &#8212; DISCONTINUED OPERATIONS</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">There were no discontinued operations as of December 31, 2019. As of December 31, 2018, discontinued operations was comprised of Business Air and residual activity of the Financial Freedom business, which was sold in May 2018. As part of the Financial Freedom Transaction, the sale of the Financial Freedom business included all the operations, mortgage servicing rights and related servicing assets and liabilities. In July 2019, CIT obtained the final investor consent from Government National Mortgage Association (&#8220;GNMA&#8221;) to transfer CIT&#8217;s servicer obligation to a third party and derecognized the assets, which had previously not met the accounting requirements for sale treatment, and related secured borrowing of approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000672" name="us-gaap:DisposalGroupIncludingDiscontinuedOperationAccountsPayableAndAccruedLiabilities" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapDisposalGroupClassificationAxis_us-gaapSegmentDiscontinuedOperationsMember_us-gaapIncomeStatementBalanceSheetAndAdditionalDisclosuresByDisposalGroupsIncludingDiscontinuedOperationsAxis_citServiceObligationMember_20190731" decimals="-6" scale="6">152</ix:nonFraction> million from the Financial Freedom business. <p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Certain of the following tables present credit-related information at the &#8220;class&#8221; level.&#160;&#160;A class is generally a disaggregation of a portfolio segment. In determining the classes, CIT considered the loan characteristics and methods it applies in monitoring and assessing credit risk and performance.</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Credit Quality Information</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Commercial obligor risk ratings are reviewed on a regular basis by Credit Risk Management and are adjusted as necessary for updated information affecting the borrowers' ability to fulfill their obligations.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The definitions of the commercial loan ratings are as follows:</p>
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:3.51%;white-space:nowrap">

If left uncorrected, these potential weaknesses may, at some future date, result in the deterioration of the repayment prospects.</p></td></tr></table></div>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;letter-spacing:-0.05pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Classified &#8212; a classified asset ranges from: (1) assets that exhibit a well-defined weakness and are inadequately protected by the current sound worth and paying capacity of the borrower and are characterized by the distinct possibility that some loss will be sustained if the deficiencies are not corrected to (2) assets with weaknesses that make collection or liquidation in full unlikely on the basis of current facts, conditions, and values. Assets in this classification can be accruing or on non- accrual depending on the evaluation of these factors.</p></td></tr></table></div></ix:nonNumeric>

<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The SFR amounts represent the carrying value, which differ from unpaid principal balances, and include the premiums or discounts and the accretable yield and non-accretable difference for PCI loans recorded in purchase accounting. Certain consumer SFR loans are &#8220;covered loans&#8221; for which the Company can be reimbursed for a portion of certain future losses. Covered loans relate to loans acquired from the OneWest Bank acquisition with indemnifications provided by the FDIC under LSAs for certain future losses. </p></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">115</p>
<p style="text-align:right;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">CIT ANNUAL REPORT 2019</p>

<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000476_dcnt_e4c6d0b0-0fb1-47c8-a5dd-54ddec333657" continuedAt="F_000476_dcnt_4537f516-b581-4010-9e7e-9f8760cf6494">
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The LSAs with the FDIC relate to the FDIC-assisted transactions of IndyMac in March 2009, First Federal in December 2009 and La Jolla Bank in February 2010. The indemnification period for IndyMac ended in March 2019. Post March 2019, the covered loans are limited to First Federal and La Jolla with the indemnification period ending in December 2019 and February 2020, respectively. <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000910" name="cit:FDICClaimFirstThreshold" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_citFirstFederalBankOfCaliforniaAndLaJollaBankMember_20190331" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="6">No</ix:nonFraction> indemnification asset was recognized in connection with First Federal and La Jolla. The Company separately recognizes a net receivable (recorded in other assets) for the claim submissions filed with the FDIC.<span style="font-size:10pt;"> </span></p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At December 31, 2019, the indemnification asset is <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000911" name="us-gaap:FDICIndemnificationAsset" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_citIndymacFederalBankMember_20191231" decimals="-6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="6">zero</ix:nonFraction>, as compared to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000912" name="us-gaap:FDICIndemnificationAsset" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_citIndymacFederalBankMember_20181231" decimals="-5" scale="6">10.8</ix:nonFraction> million at December 31, 2018 and there was a net receivable from the FDIC of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000913" name="cit:FDICIndemnificationAssetReceivable" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_citIndymacFederalBankMember_20191231" decimals="-6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="6">zero</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000914" name="cit:FDICIndemnificationAssetReceivable" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_citIndymacFederalBankMember_20181231" decimals="-5" scale="6">6.4</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively. Apart from the loss share reimbursements from the FDIC, the decline in the indemnification asset during 2018 reflects the reduction in the indemnification receivable from the FDIC related to covered servicer-related obligations for reverse mortgages from $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000915" name="us-gaap:FDICIndemnificationAssetCashPaymentsReceived" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_citIndymacFederalBankMember_20180101_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6">29</ix:nonFraction> million to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000916" name="us-gaap:FDICIndemnificationAssetCashPaymentsReceived" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_citIndymacFederalBankMember_20170101_20171231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">zero</ix:nonFraction>, an impairment charge of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000917" name="us-gaap:FDICIndemnificationAssetNetWriteOffs" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_citIndymacFederalBankMember_20180101_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6">21</ix:nonFraction> million and amortization of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000918" name="cit:FDICIndemnificationAssetAmortization" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_citIndymacFederalBankMember_20180101_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6">40</ix:nonFraction> million. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the year ended December 31, 2018, CIT performed a collectability assessment of the probable losses to be reimbursed by the FDIC given the significantly shorter remaining life of the indemnification asset in comparison to the weighted average life of the related covered loans and significant decline in loss share claims filed with the FDIC. Separate from the higher negative yield to amortize the reductions in expected indemnification asset cash flows due to an increase in expected cash flows on the covered loans from improved credit performance, CIT recorded an impairment of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000919" name="us-gaap:FDICIndemnificationAssetNetWriteOffs" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapIncomeStatementLocationAxis_us-gaapOtherIncomeMember_20180101_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6">21</ix:nonFraction> million in other noninterest income for the amounts deemed uncollectable within the remaining indemnification period based on CIT&#8217;s loan level review of the covered loans.&#160;&#160;</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Impairment occurs when, based on current information and events, it is probable that CIT will be unable to collect all amounts due according to contractual terms of the agreement. For commercial loans, the Company has established review and monitoring procedures designed to identify, as early as possible, customers that are experiencing financial difficulty. Credit risk is captured and analyzed based on the Company's PD and LGD ratings. A PD rating is determined by evaluating borrower credit-worthiness, including analyzing credit history, financial condition, cash flow adequacy, financial performance and management quality. An LGD rating is predicated on transaction structure, collateral valuation and related guarantees or recourse. Further, related considerations in determining probability of collection include the following:</p>

<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Loans Acquired with Deteriorated Credit Quality</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company applied the income recognition and disclosure guidance in ASC 310-30 to loans that were identified as PCI as of the Acquisition Date. PCI loans were initially recorded at estimated fair value with no allowance for loan losses carried over, since the initial fair values reflected credit losses expected to be incurred over the remaining lives of the loans. <p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Non-criticized loans generally include loans that are expected to be repaid in accordance with contractual loan terms. Criticized loans are risk rated as special mention or classified.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Accretable Yield</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The excess of cash flows expected to be collected over the recorded investment (estimated fair value at acquisition) of the PCI loans represents the accretable yield and is recognized in interest income on an effective yield basis over the remaining life of the loan, or pools of loans. The accretable yield is adjusted for changes in interest rate indices for variable rate PCI loans, changes in prepayment assumptions and changes in expected principal and interest payments and collateral values. Further, if a loan within a pool of loans is modified, the modified loan remains part of the pool of loans.</p></ix:continuation>

<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Troubled Debt Restructuring</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company periodically modifies the terms of loans in response to borrowers&#8217; difficulties. Modifications that include a financial concession to the borrower are accounted for as TDRs.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">A restructuring of a debt constitutes a TDR for purposes of ASC 310-40, if CIT, for economic or legal reasons related to the debtor&#8217;s financial difficulties, grants a concession to the debtor that it would not otherwise consider. A concession either stems from an agreement between CIT and the debtor or is imposed by law or a court of law.&#160; One key indicator of a concession is the lender granting a term or condition that it would not ordinarily consider, such as accepting assets other than cash in partial settlement of the obligation. Another key indicator of a concession is the lender agreeing to a term or condition that is below market, such as lowering the interest rate or agreeing to convert scheduled cash pay interest to Payment in Kind (&#8220;PIK&#8221;).&#8221;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">A TDR may include, but is not limited to, one or a combination of the following:</p>

<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:3.51%;white-space:nowrap">

<td valign="top" style="width:3.51%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-size:9pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">

This includes a transfer resulting from foreclosure or repossession.</span></p></td></tr></table></div>

<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The financial impact of the various modification strategies that the Company employs in response to borrower difficulties is presented below. Although the focus is on the December 31, 2019 amounts, the overall nature and impact of modification programs were comparable in the prior year.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Modifications qualifying as TDRs based upon recorded investment at December 31, 2019 were comprised of payment deferrals (<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001287" name="cit:TroubledDebtRestructuringPaymentDeferralRate" contextRef="C_0001171825_20191231" decimals="2" scale="-2">52</ix:nonFraction>%) and covenant relief and/or other (<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001289" name="cit:TroubledDebtRestructuringCovenantReliefRateOther" contextRef="C_0001171825_20191231" decimals="2" scale="-2">48</ix:nonFraction>%).&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2018, TDR recorded investment was comprised of payment deferrals (<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001288" name="cit:TroubledDebtRestructuringPaymentDeferralRate" contextRef="C_0001171825_20181231" decimals="2" scale="-2">51</ix:nonFraction>%) and covenant relief and/or other (<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001290" name="cit:TroubledDebtRestructuringCovenantReliefRateOther" contextRef="C_0001171825_20181231" decimals="2" scale="-2">49</ix:nonFraction>%).</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The components of lease expense are recorded in Operating expenses. Variable lease cost includes common area maintenance, property taxes, and other operating expenses related to leased premises. Sublease income results from leasing excess building space that CIT is no longer utilizing under operating leases which have remaining lease terms of up to <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001409" name="cit:LesseeOperatingLeaseSubleaseRemainingLeaseTerm" contextRef="C_0001171825_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20190101_20191231" format="ixt-sec:duryear">2</ix:nonNumeric> years.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Lessor</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company leases equipment to commercial end-users under operating lease and finance lease arrangements. The majority of operating lease equipment is long-lived rail equipment which is typically leased several times over the equipment&#8217;s life. We also lease technology and office equipment and large and small industrial, medical, and transportation equipment under both operating leases and finance leases.&#160;&#160; </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our Rail operating leases typically do not include purchase options. Many of our finance leases, and other equipment operating leases, offer the lessee the option to purchase the equipment at fair market value or for a nominal fixed purchase option&#59; and many of the leases that do not have a nominal purchase option include renewal provisions resulting in some leases continuing beyond initial contractual term. Our leases typically do not include early termination options&#59; and continued rent payments are due if leased equipment is not returned at the end of the lease.</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000557" name="cit:NetBookValueOfOperatingLeaseEquipmentByEquipmentTypeTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001171825_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000557_cnt_1">

<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As discussed in <span style="font-style:italic;">Note 1 &#8212; Business and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</span>, the Company conducted and documented its periodic review of all securities with unrealized losses, which it performs to evaluate whether the impairment is other than temporary. <p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">There were <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001668" name="us-gaap:OtherThanTemporaryImpairmentLossesInvestmentsPortionInOtherComprehensiveIncomeLossBeforeTaxIncludingPortionAttributableToNoncontrollingInterest" contextRef="C_0001171825_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="6">no</ix:nonFraction> OTTI losses recognized for the year ended December 31, 2019. <p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTE 9 &#8212; VARIABLE INTEREST ENTITIES</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Variable Interest Entities</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Described below are the results of the Company&#8217;s assessment of its variable interests in order to determine its current status with regards to being the VIE PB. See <span style="font-style:italic;">Note 1 &#8212; Business and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</span> for additional information on accounting for VIEs. </p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Consolidated VIEs</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At December 31, 2019 and 2018, there were <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_citEntity" id="F_001718" name="cit:NumberOfConsolidatedVariableInterestEntities" contextRef="C_0001171825_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_citEntity" id="F_001719" name="cit:NumberOfConsolidatedVariableInterestEntities" contextRef="C_0001171825_20181231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">no</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> consolidated VIEs. </p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Unconsolidated VIEs</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Unconsolidated VIEs include agency and non-agency securitization structures, limited partnership interests and joint ventures where the Company&#8217;s involvement is limited to an investor interest and the Company does not have the power to direct the activities of the VIE that most significantly impact the VIE&#8217;s economic performance or obligation to absorb losses or the right to receive benefits that could potentially be significant to the VIE.</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In connection with the sale of Financial Freedom in 2018, CIT transferred the economic benefit and risk of the HECM loans and the GNMA HMBS securitizations to the buyer, but continued to act as master servicer. At December 31, 2018, these were VIEs for which CIT was not the PB and which were reported in discontinued operations. At December 31, 2019, there were <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_citEntity" id="F_001720" name="cit:NumberOfConsolidatedVariableInterestEntities" contextRef="C_0001171825_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">no</ix:nonFraction> VIEs in Discontinued Operations as CIT transferred the servicer obligation to a third party upon receiving the GNMA consent. See <span style="font-style:italic;">Note 2 &#8212; Discontinued Operations.</span></p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000571" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfVariableInterestEntitiesTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001171825_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000571_cnt_1">

The Company believes the possibility is remote under this hypothetical scenario&#59; accordingly, this required disclosure is not an indication of expected loss.</p></ix:nonNumeric></ix:nonNumeric>

<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Unsecured Borrowings</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Revolving Credit Facility</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Revolving Credit Facility had a total commitment amount of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001774" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_20191231" decimals="INF" scale="6">400</ix:nonFraction> million at December 31, 2019, which was reduced from a total commitment amount of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001775" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_20181231" decimals="INF" scale="6">500</ix:nonFraction> million at December 31, 2018. The applicable margin charged under the facility is <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001776" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentBasisSpreadOnVariableRate1" contextRef="C_0001171825_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_us-gaapVariableRateAxis_us-gaapLondonInterbankOfferedRateLIBORMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">2.00</ix:nonFraction>% for LIBOR Rate loans and <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001777" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentBasisSpreadOnVariableRate1" contextRef="C_0001171825_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_us-gaapVariableRateAxis_us-gaapBaseRateMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">1.00</ix:nonFraction>% for Base Rate loans. The final maturity date of the lenders&#8217; commitments is <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001780" name="cit:ExtendedLineOfCreditFacilityExpirationDate1" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_20190101_20190331" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">March 1, 2021</ix:nonNumeric>. </p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Revolving Credit Facility includes a covenant that requires that the Company maintain a minimum Tier 1 capital ratio of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001778" name="us-gaap:TierOneRiskBasedCapitalRequiredForCapitalAdequacyToRiskWeightedAssets" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_20170404" decimals="INF" scale="-2">9.0</ix:nonFraction>%.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2019, the Revolving Credit Facility was unsecured and was guaranteed by <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_citsubsidiary" id="F_001779" name="cit:NumberOfDomesticOperatingSubsidiariesThatAreGuarantors" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">three</ix:nonFraction> of the Company&#8217;s domestic operating subsidiaries. In addition, the applicable required minimum guarantor asset coverage ratio ranged from <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_001781_2">1.0:1.0</span> to <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_001782_2">1.5:1.0</span>, and was <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_001783_2">1.25:1.00</span> at December 31, 2019.  </p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Revolving<span style="font-size:10pt;"> </span>Credit Facility may be drawn, prepaid and redrawn at the option of CIT. The unutilized portion of any commitment under the Revolving Credit Facility may be reduced permanently or terminated by CIT at any time without penalty. The $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001785" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">400</ix:nonFraction> million total commitment amount consisted of a $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001786" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_citRevolvingCreditFacilityNotLetterofCreditMember_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">300</ix:nonFraction> million revolving loan tranche and a $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001787" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapLetterOfCreditMember_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">100</ix:nonFraction> million revolving loan tranche that can also be utilized for issuance of letters of credit.
