<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Secured Borrowings</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At December 31, 2019, the Company had pledged $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001819" name="cit:PledgedAssets" contextRef="C_0001171825_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">11.3</ix:nonFraction> billion of assets (including collateral for the FRB discount window that is currently not drawn). Effective April 5, 2019, the FHLB released its blanket lien covering approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001821" name="cit:FederalHomeLoanBankReleasedBlanketLienCoveringBookValueOfAssets" contextRef="C_0001171825_20190405" decimals="-5" scale="6">18.9</ix:nonFraction> billion (book value) of CIT Bank assets.&#160;At December 31, 2019, the collateral specifically identified and used to calculate available borrowings was $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001820" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentCollateralAmount" contextRef="C_0001171825_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">11.3</ix:nonFraction> billion, which included $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001822" name="us-gaap:PledgedFinancialInstrumentsNotSeparatelyReportedLoansReceivablePledgedAsCollateral" contextRef="C_0001171825_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">11.2</ix:nonFraction> billion of loans and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001823" name="cit:PledgedAssetsCash" contextRef="C_0001171825_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">0.1</ix:nonFraction> billion of cash and cash equivalents. Under the FHLB Facility, CIT Bank, N.A. may at any time grant a security interest in, sell, convey or otherwise dispose of any of the assets used for collateral, provided that CIT Bank, N.A. is in compliance with the collateral maintenance requirement immediately following such disposition and all other requirements of the facility at the time of such disposition.</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">FHLB Advances</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As a member of the FHLB of San Francisco, CIT Bank N.A. can access financing based on an evaluation of its creditworthiness, statement of financial position, size and eligibility of collateral. The interest rates charged by the FHLB for advances typically vary depending upon maturity, the cost of funds of the FHLB, and the collateral provided for the borrowing. Advances are secured by certain Bank assets and bear either a fixed or floating interest rate. The FHLB advances are collateralized by a variety of consumer and commercial loans, including SFR mortgage loans, multi-family mortgage loans, commercial real estate loans, certain foreclosed properties and certain amounts receivable under the IndyMac LSA with the FDIC, which expired in March 2019.</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of December 31, 2019, the Company had $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001824" name="us-gaap:FederalHomeLoanBankAdvancesGeneralDebtObligationsDisclosuresMaximumAmountAvailable" contextRef="C_0001171825_20191231" decimals="-8" scale="9">6.4</ix:nonFraction> billion of financing capacity with the FHLB, of which $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001825" name="us-gaap:FederalHomeLoanBankAdvancesGeneralDebtObligationsDisclosuresAmountOfAvailableUnusedFunds" contextRef="C_0001171825_20191231" decimals="-8" scale="9">4.7</ix:nonFraction> billion was unused and available. <p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000484" name="us-gaap:DerivativeInstrumentsAndHedgingActivitiesDisclosureTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001171825_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000484_dcnt_7e4d013f-7488-49f0-ab70-d2ac8e3d0115">
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTE 11 &#8212; DERIVATIVE FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As part of managing exposure to interest rate and foreign currency risk, the Company enters into derivative transactions with other financial institutions. The Company also enters into derivative contracts with customers as part of its Commercial Banking business. The Company does not enter into derivative contracts for proprietary trading or speculative purposes.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">See <span style="font-style:italic;">Note 1 &#8212; Business and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</span>, for the description of the Company&#8217;s derivative products and transaction policies.</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000576" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfNotionalAmountsOfOutstandingDerivativePositionsTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001171825_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000576_dcnt_c685ed2c-0f40-4490-9774-be3a8b42b2ef">
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The following table presents fair values and notional values of derivative financial instruments, which includes the gross amounts of recognized financial assets and liabilities&#59; the amounts offset in the consolidated balance sheet&#59; the net amounts presented in the consolidated balance sheet&#59; the amounts subject to an enforceable master netting arrangement or similar agreement that were not included in the offset<span style="font-size:10pt;"> </span>amount above, and the amount of cash collateral received or pledged:</p></ix:nonNumeric></ix:nonNumeric>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">TRS Facility</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Two of CIT&#8217;s wholly-owned subsidiaries, one Canadian, CIT Financial Ltd. (&#8220;CFL&#8221;) and one Dutch, CIT TRS Funding B.V. (&#8220;BV&#8221;),</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">were each party to a financing facility (the &#8220;Canadian TRS Facility&#8221; and the &#8220;Dutch TRS Facility&#8221;, respectively) that were</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">structured as TRS with Goldman Sachs International (&#8220;GSI&#8221;). Under each TRS, the amount available for advances (otherwise known as the unused portion) was accounted for as a derivative financial instrument and recorded at its respective estimated fair value.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000486" name="us-gaap:FairValueDisclosuresTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001171825_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000486_dcnt_62904e91-f317-4433-b9a3-cd26babacc48">
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTE 13 &#8212; FAIR VALUE</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Fair Value Hierarchy</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company measures certain financial assets and liabilities at fair value. Fair value is defined as the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. U.S. GAAP also establishes a fair value hierarchy, which prioritizes the inputs to valuation techniques used to measure fair value into three levels. See <span style="font-style:italic;">Note 1 &#8212; Business and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</span> for a description of the Company's valuation process for assets and liabilities measured at fair value and fair value hierarchy.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Disclosures that follow in this note exclude assets and liabilities classified as discontinued operations.</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">133</p>
<p style="text-align:right;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">CIT ANNUAL REPORT 2019</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The methods and assumptions used to estimate the fair value of each class of financial instruments measured at fair value on a recurring basis are as follows:</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Debt securities AFS <span style="font-style:normal;">&#8212;Investments in U.S. government agency and sponsored agency guaranteed</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;"> </span><span style="font-style:normal;">mortgage-backed securities, U.S. government agency and sponsored agency obligations, U.S. Treasury securities and supranational securities were valued using Level 2 inputs. The market for certain corporate bonds is not active, therefore the estimated fair value was determined using a discounted cash flow technique. Given the lack of observable market data, the estimated fair value of the corporate bonds was classified as Level 3. See </span>Note 1 &#8211; Business and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies<span style="font-style:normal;"> for details on significant inputs and valuation techniques.</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Securities carried at fair value with changes recorded in net income<span style="font-style:normal;"> &#8212; Most equity securities were valued using Level 2 inputs based on published net asset value, with the remaining securities being valued using Level 1 inputs. </span></p></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">134</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">CIT ANNUAL REPORT 2019</p>

<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000486_dcnt_bb03e500-2b74-4339-8048-92e3a3ffcc64" continuedAt="F_000486_dcnt_66d52b44-414d-4ddc-9198-a613642c4a73">
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Derivative Assets and Liabilities</span><span style="font-style:normal;"> &#8212;</span><span style="font-style:normal;"> </span><span style="font-style:normal;">Derivatives were valued using models that incorporate inputs depending on the type of derivative. Besides the fair value of credit derivatives, which were estimated using Level 3 inputs, most derivative instruments were valued using Level 2 inputs based on quoted prices for similar assets and liabilities and model-based valuation techniques for which all significant assumptions are observable in the market. See </span><span style="font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Note 1 &#8211; </span><span style="font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Business and </span><span style="font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</span><span style="font-style:normal;"> for details on significant inputs and valuation techniques. See </span><span style="font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Note 11 &#8212; Derivative Financial Instruments</span><span style="font-style:normal;"> for notional principal amounts and fair values.</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">FDIC True-up Liability<span style="font-style:normal;"> &#8212; The FDIC True-up liability was recorded at estimated fair value as of the date of the OneWest Transaction related to the FDIC-assisted transaction of La Jolla and is measured at fair value at each reporting date until the contingency is resolved. Due to the significant unobservable inputs used, these measurements were classified as Level 3.</span></p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000582" name="us-gaap:FairValueAssetsAndLiabilitiesMeasuredOnRecurringAndNonrecurringBasisValuationTechniquesTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001171825_20190101_20191231" escape="true">

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:8pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Assets Measured at Fair Value on a Non-recurring Basis</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Certain assets or liabilities are required to be measured at estimated fair value on a non-recurring basis subsequent to initial recognition. Generally, these adjustments are the result of LOCOM or other impairment accounting. In determining the estimated fair values, the Company determined that substantially all the changes in estimated fair value were due to declines in market conditions versus instrument specific credit risk. This was determined by examining the changes in market factors relative to instrument specific factors.</p></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">135</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The methods and assumptions used to estimate the fair value of each class of financial instruments not measured at fair value are as follows:</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Assets Held for Sale<span style="font-style:normal;"> &#8211; See </span>Carrying Value of Assets Measured at Fair Value on a Non-recurring Basis<span style="font-style:normal;"> above in this note for fair value measurements of AHFS.</span> </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Loans</p>
<div style="align:left;">

<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-style:italic;">Commercial and Consumer Loans</span> &#8212; Commercial and consumer loans are generally valued individually. As there is no liquid secondary market for most loans, the fair value was primarily estimated based on analysis that used significant Level 3 inputs at both December 31, 2019 and December 31, 2018. See <span style="font-style:italic;">Note 1 &#8211; Business and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</span> for details on significant inputs and valuation techniques.</p></td></tr></table></div>

<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-style:italic;">PCI loans</span> &#8212; These loans were valued by separating the loans into performing and non-performing groups and stratifying them based on common risk characteristics such as product type, FICO score and other economic attributes. Due to the significance of the unobservable inputs, these loans are classified as Level 3.</p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Securities Purchased Under Agreement to Resell<span style="font-style:normal;"> &#8211; The fair value of securities purchased under agreement to resell was determined using a discount cash flow technique. Interest rates appropriate to the maturity and underlying collateral are used for discounting the estimated cash flows. As observable market interest rates are used, the fair value of securities purchased under agreement to resell was classified as Level 2.</span></p></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">137</p>
<p style="text-align:right;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">CIT ANNUAL REPORT 2019</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000486_dcnt_410201e4-d1d3-4587-b5fe-3a9b06e1befc">
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Investment Securities</span></p>
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:3.51%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#9642; </span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-style:italic;">Non-marketable securities</span> - Utilize Level 3 inputs to estimate fair value and were generally recorded under the cost method of accounting. FHLB and FRB stock carrying values approximate fair value. Of the remaining non-marketable securities, the fair value is determined based on techniques that use significant assumptions that are not observable in the market. </p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Deposits<span style="font-style:normal;"> &#8212; The estimated fair value of deposits with no stated maturity, such as demand deposit accounts, money market accounts, and savings accounts was the amount payable on demand at the reporting date.</span> <span style="font-style:normal;">The fair value of time deposits is estimated using Level 3 inputs.</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Borrowings</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Level 2 fair value of borrowings were calculated using market inputs and discounted value of the contractual cash flows using current estimated market discount rates for borrowings with similar terms, remaining maturities and put dates and did not require significant judgment<span style="font-style:italic;">.</span> These borrowings included:</p>
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="NOTE_15___REGULATORY_CAPITAL">NOTE 15 &#8212; REGULATORY CAPITAL</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company and the Bank are each subject to various regulatory capital requirements administered by the FRB and the OCC. Quantitative measures established by regulation to ensure capital adequacy require that the Company and the Bank each maintain minimum amounts and ratios of Total, Tier 1 and Common Equity Tier 1 capital to risk-weighted assets, and of Tier 1 capital to average assets. We compute capital ratios in accordance with Federal Reserve capital guidelines and OCC capital guidelines for assessing adequacy of capital for the Company and CIT Bank, respectively. The regulatory capital guidelines applicable to the Company and Bank were the Basel III Rule and the Transition Final Rule (effective January 1, 2018 to extend the regulatory capital treatment under 2017 transition provisions for certain items). </p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000589" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfComplianceWithRegulatoryCapitalRequirementsUnderBankingRegulationsTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001171825_20190101_20191231" escape="true">

This includes: (1) a DTA of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002828" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsNet" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapInternalRevenueServiceIRSMember_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">387.2</ix:nonFraction> million relating to its cumulative U.S. federal NOLs of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002829" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapInternalRevenueServiceIRSMember_20191231" decimals="-8" scale="9">1.9</ix:nonFraction> billion&#59; (2) DTAs of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002831" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsNet" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapStateAndLocalJurisdictionMember_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">287.0</ix:nonFraction> million relating to cumulative state NOLs of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002832" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapStateAndLocalJurisdictionMember_20191231" decimals="-8" scale="9">5.0</ix:nonFraction> billion, including amounts of reporting entities that file in multiple jurisdictions, and (3) DTAs of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002834" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsNet" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapForeignCountryMember_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">12.0</ix:nonFraction> million relating to cumulative non-U.S. NOLs of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002835" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapForeignCountryMember_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">47.3</ix:nonFraction> million. However, a VA of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002838" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwardsValuationAllowance" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapStateAndLocalJurisdictionMember_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">183.2</ix:nonFraction> million was retained on U.S. state DTAs on certain NOLs as of December&#160;31, 2019. </p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During 2017, the Company reported a net $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002839" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapInternalRevenueServiceIRSMember_20170101_20171231" decimals="-5" scale="6">177.4</ix:nonFraction> million U.S. income tax benefit comprised of a gross $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002840" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsGross" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapInternalRevenueServiceIRSMember_20171231" decimals="-5" scale="6">234.2</ix:nonFraction> million tax benefit on a capital loss of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002841" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsCapitalLossCarryforwards" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapInternalRevenueServiceIRSMember_20171231" decimals="-5" scale="6">610.5</ix:nonFraction> million realized on the liquidation of a wholly-owned foreign subsidiary partially offset by a $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002842" name="cit:PartiallyOffsetOfValuationAllowanceAgainstUnusedPortionOfCapitalLoss" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapInternalRevenueServiceIRSMember_20170101_20171231" decimals="-5" scale="6">56.8</ix:nonFraction> million charge to establish a VA against the unused portion of the capital loss. As a result of the change in the U.S. Federal income tax rate from <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_002843" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateReconciliationAtFederalStatutoryIncomeTaxRate" contextRef="C_0001171825_20170101_20171231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">35</ix:nonFraction> percent to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_002844" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateReconciliationAtFederalStatutoryIncomeTaxRate" contextRef="C_0001171825_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">21</ix:nonFraction> percent beginning in 2018, the VA against the capital loss carryforwards was revalued to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002845" name="cit:CapitalLossCarryforwardValuationAllowance" contextRef="C_0001171825_20171231" decimals="-5" scale="6">39.6</ix:nonFraction> million as of December 31, 2017. During 2019, the Company released the remaining $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002847" name="cit:CapitalLossCarryforwardValuationAllowance" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapInternalRevenueServiceIRSMember_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">9.0</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002848" name="cit:CapitalLossCarryforwardValuationAllowance" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapStateAndLocalJurisdictionMember_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">1.5</ix:nonFraction> million of U.S. federal and state VA, respectively, on the DTA established on capital loss carryforwards, down from $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002846" name="cit:CapitalLossCarryforwardValuationAllowance" contextRef="C_0001171825_20181231" decimals="-5" scale="6">10.5</ix:nonFraction> million in 2018. The reduction was attributable to net capital gains recognized in 2019 in the normal course of business.&#160;&#160;Additionally, the Company generated $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002849" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsCapitalLossCarryforwards" contextRef="C_0001171825_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">2.5</ix:nonFraction> million of net capital losses during 2019 from the impairment of LIHTC investments which was partially offset by a $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002850" name="cit:PartiallyOffsetOfValuationAllowanceAgainstUnusedPortionOfCapitalLoss" contextRef="C_0001171825_20190101_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">0.5</ix:nonFraction> million VA against the unused portion of the capital loss. The Company will recognize the income tax benefit on the remaining portion of the DTA subject to the VA to the extent of additional capital gains. Capital losses can be carried forward for <ix:nonNumeric id="F_002851" name="cit:CapitalLossesCarryForwardPeriodInYears" contextRef="C_0001171825_20170101_20171231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">five years</ix:nonNumeric> to offset future capital gains but require a VA until additional capital gains are identified.</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company maintained a VA of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002852" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowance" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapForeignCountryMember_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">14.8</ix:nonFraction> million against certain non-U.S. reporting entities' net DTAs at December&#160;31, 2019, down from $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002853" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowance" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapForeignCountryMember_20181231" decimals="-5" scale="6">18.0</ix:nonFraction> million at December&#160;31, 2018. The decrease is mainly related to the write-off of DTAs for certain reporting entities due to the remote likelihood that they will ever utilize their respective DTAs.</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company's ability to recognize DTAs is evaluated on a quarterly basis to determine if there are any significant events that would affect our ability to utilize existing DTAs. If events are identified that affect our ability to utilize our DTAs, VAs may be adjusted accordingly.</p></ix:continuation>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the year ended December&#160;31, 2019, the Company recorded a net $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002874" name="us-gaap:UnrecognizedTaxBenefitsPeriodIncreaseDecrease" contextRef="C_0001171825_20190101_20191231" decimals="-5" sign="-" scale="6">0.8</ix:nonFraction> million decrease in unrecognized tax benefits ("UTBs"), including interest and penalties. The majority of the net decrease is related to the reversal of a position in a foreign jurisdiction due to the expiration of the statute of limitations partially offset by the establishment of a new position related to the recognition of certain state NOLs.</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the year ended December&#160;31, 2019, the Company recognized $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002875" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExaminationPenaltiesAndInterestExpense" contextRef="C_0001171825_20190101_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">0.4</ix:nonFraction> million income tax benefit relating to interest and penalties on its UTBs. The change in balance is mainly related to the reversal of interest and penalties associated with the above mentioned UTBs taken on a prior year Canadian position due to the expiration of statute of limitations.&#160;&#160;As of December&#160;31, 2019, the accrued liability for interest and penalties is $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002876" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExaminationPenaltiesAndInterestAccrued" contextRef="C_0001171825_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">6.5</ix:nonFraction> million. The Company recognizes accrued interest and penalties on UTBs in income tax expense.</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The entire $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002877" name="us-gaap:UnrecognizedTaxBenefits" contextRef="C_0001171825_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">19.9</ix:nonFraction> million of UTBs including interest and penalties at December&#160;31, 2019, would lower the Company's effective tax rate, if realized. Management believes that it is reasonably possible the total potential liability before interest and penalties may be increased or decreased by $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002878" name="cit:IncreaseDecreaseInUnrecognizedTaxBenefitsIsReasonablyPossible" contextRef="C_0001171825_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">10</ix:nonFraction> million within the next twelve months of the reporting date because of anticipated settlement with taxing authorities, resolution of open tax matters, and the expiration of various statutes of limitations.</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Income Tax Audits</p>

<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company and its subsidiaries are under examination in various states, provinces and countries for years ranging from 2012 through 2017. <p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTE 20 &#8212; RETIREMENT, POSTRETIREMENT AND OTHER BENEFIT PLANS</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">CIT provides various benefit programs, including defined benefit retirement and postretirement plans, and defined contribution savings incentive plans. A summary of major plans is provided below.</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Retirement and Postretirement Benefit Plans</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:3.51%;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Retirement Benefits</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">CIT maintains a frozen U.S. non-contributory pension plan (the "Plan") qualified under the Internal Revenue Code (&#8220;IRC&#8221;).&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company also maintains a frozen U.S. non-contributory supplemental retirement plan (the "Supplemental Plan&#8221;), and an Executive Retirement Plan, which has been closed to new members since 2006, and whose participants are all inactive as of December&#160;31, 2018. </p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">145</p>
<p style="text-align:right;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">CIT ANNUAL REPORT 2019</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000493_dcnt_7445d533-75be-4585-acb1-12eb606dd5c0" continuedAt="F_000493_dcnt_2e590271-9354-4dfe-8fae-6459c5d3c73f">
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Accumulated balances under the Plan and the Supplemental Plan continue to receive periodic interest, subject to certain government limits. The interest credit was <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_002883" name="cit:DefinedBenefitsPlanBenefitsPayToParticipantsPercentageInterestCredit" contextRef="C_0001171825_20190101_20191231" decimals="4" scale="-2">2.98</ix:nonFraction>%, <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_002884" name="cit:DefinedBenefitsPlanBenefitsPayToParticipantsPercentageInterestCredit" contextRef="C_0001171825_20180101_20181231" decimals="4" scale="-2">2.60</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_002885" name="cit:DefinedBenefitsPlanBenefitsPayToParticipantsPercentageInterestCredit" contextRef="C_0001171825_20170101_20171231" decimals="4" scale="-2">2.84</ix:nonFraction>% for the years ended December&#160;31, 2019, 2018 and 2017, respectively.</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:3.51%;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Postretirement Benefits</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">CIT provides healthcare and life insurance benefits to eligible retired employees. For most eligible retirees, healthcare is contributory and life insurance is non-contributory. All postretirement benefit plans are funded on a pay-as-you-go basis.</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company amended CIT's postretirement benefit plans to discontinue benefits effective December 31, 2012. CIT no longer offers retiree medical, dental and life insurance benefits to those who did not meet the eligibility criteria for these benefits by December 31, 2013. </p>

<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Discount rate assumptions used for pension and post-retirement benefit plan accounting reflect prevailing rates available on high-quality, fixed-income debt instruments with maturities that match the benefit obligation.</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Expected long-term rate of return assumptions on assets are based on projected asset allocation and historical and expected future returns for each asset class. Independent analysis of historical and projected asset returns, inflation, and interest rates are provided by the Company's investment consultants and actuaries as part of the Company's assumptions process.</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000602" name="cit:BenefitPlanWeightedAverageAssumptionsUsedInMeasurementOfBenefitObligationsTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001171825_20190101_20191231" escape="true">

<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Plan investments are stated at fair value. Common stock traded on security exchanges as well as mutual funds, exchange traded funds and short term investment funds are valued at closing market prices. Such investments are considered Level 1 per fair value hierarchy. Investments in Common Collective Trusts and Alternative Investment Funds are carried at fair value based upon reported net asset values ("NAV"). </p></ix:continuation>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Savings Incentive Plan</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">CIT has defined contribution retirement plans covering certain of its U.S. employees which qualify under section 401(k) of the Internal Revenue Code. Employees may contribute a portion of their eligible compensation, as defined, subject to regulatory limits and plan provisions, and the Company matches these contributions up to a threshold. Participants are also eligible for an additional discretionary company contribution. The cost of these plans totaled $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_003075" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanCostRecognized" contextRef="C_0001171825_20190101_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">20.5</ix:nonFraction> million, $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_003076" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanCostRecognized" contextRef="C_0001171825_20180101_20181231" decimals="-5" scale="6">19.2</ix:nonFraction> million, and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_003077" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanCostRecognized" contextRef="C_0001171825_20170101_20171231" decimals="-5" scale="6">18.7</ix:nonFraction> million for the years ended December&#160;31, 2019, 2018 and 2017, respectively.</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Stock-Based Compensation</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In February 2016, the Company adopted the CIT Group Inc. 2016 Omnibus Incentive Plan (the "2016 Plan"), which provides for grants of stock-based awards to employees, executive officers and directors, and replaced the Amended and Restated CIT Group Inc. Long-Term Incentive Plan (the "Prior Plan"). The number of shares of common stock that may be issued for all purposes under the 2016 Plan is (1) <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_003078" name="cit:SharebasedCompensationArrangementbySharebasedPaymentAwardNumberofSharesAuthorizedSharesAuthorizedUnderNewPlan" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_citOmnibusIncentivePlan2016PlanMember_20160229" decimals="INF" scale="6">5</ix:nonFraction> million shares plus (2) the number of authorized shares remaining available under the Prior Plan plus (3) the number of shares relating to awards granted under the Prior Plan that subsequently are forfeited, expire, terminate or otherwise lapse or are settled for cash, in whole or in part, as provided by the 2016 Plan. At December 31, 2019, the total number of shares that may be issued under the 2016 Plan was <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_003079" name="cit:SharebasedCompensationArrangementbySharebasedPaymentAwardNumberofSharesAuthorizedSharesAuthorizedUnderNewPlan" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_citOmnibusIncentivePlan2016PlanMember_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">3,733,327</ix:nonFraction> (excludes <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_003080" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsOutstandingNumber" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_citOmnibusIncentivePlan2016PlanMember_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">2,014,049</ix:nonFraction> shares underlying outstanding awards granted to employees and/or directors that are unvested and/or unsettled). Currently under the 2016 Plan, the issued and unvested awards consist mainly of Restricted Stock Units ("RSUs") and Performance Stock Units ("PSUs").</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The fair value of RSUs and PSUs are based on the fair market value of CIT's common stock on the date of grant. Compensation expense is recognized over the vesting period or the requisite service period, which is generally <ix:nonNumeric id="F_003081" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingPeriod1" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapRestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_20190101_20191231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">three years</ix:nonNumeric> for RSUs, under the graded vesting method, whereby each vesting tranche of the award is amortized separately as if each were a separate award. Compensation expense for PSUs that cliff vest are recognized over the vesting period, which is generally <ix:nonNumeric id="F_003082" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingPeriod1" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapPerformanceSharesMember_20190101_20191231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">three years</ix:nonNumeric>, and on a straight-line basis.</p></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">148</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">CIT ANNUAL REPORT 2019</p>

<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000493_dcnt_4da0dc6e-6dda-483b-a3ed-48417dd0ecfc" continuedAt="F_000493_dcnt_09a0fa22-2ce2-422b-8b73-7737759570f2">
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Operating expenses includes $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_003083" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" contextRef="C_0001171825_20190101_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">44.2</ix:nonFraction> million of compensation expense related to equity-based awards granted to employees or members of the Board of Directors for the year ended December&#160;31, 2019, including $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_003086" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapRestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">43.8</ix:nonFraction> million related to restricted and retention stock and unit awards and the remaining related to stock purchases. Compensation expense related to equity-based awards included $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_003084" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" contextRef="C_0001171825_20180101_20181231" decimals="-5" scale="6">38.8</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_003085" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" contextRef="C_0001171825_20170101_20171231" decimals="-5" scale="6">41.9</ix:nonFraction> million for the years ended December 31, 2018 and 2017, respectively. Total unrecognized compensation cost related to nonvested awards was $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_003087" name="us-gaap:EmployeeServiceShareBasedCompensationNonvestedAwardsTotalCompensationCostNotYetRecognized" contextRef="C_0001171825_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">26.1</ix:nonFraction> million at December&#160;31, 2019. This cost is expected to be recognized over a weighted average period of <ix:nonNumeric id="F_003088" name="cit:EmployeeServiceShareBasedCompensationNonvestedAwardsTotalCompensationCostNotYetRecognizedRecognizedInWeightedAveragePeriodYears" contextRef="C_0001171825_20190101_20191231" format="ixt-sec:duryear">1.87</ix:nonNumeric> years.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:3.51%;text-indent:-3.51%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Employee Stock Purchase Plan</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Eligibility for participation in the Employee Stock Purchase Plan (&#8220;ESPP&#8221;) includes employees of CIT and its participating subsidiaries, except that any employees designated as highly compensated are not eligible to participate in the ESPP. Under the ESPP, CIT is authorized to issue up to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_003089" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAuthorized" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapEmployeeStockMember_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">2,000,000</ix:nonFraction> shares of common stock to eligible employees. Eligible employees can choose to have between <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_003090" name="cit:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardMinimumEmployeeSubscriptionRate" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapEmployeeStockMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">1</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_003091" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardMaximumEmployeeSubscriptionRate" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapEmployeeStockMember_20191231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">10</ix:nonFraction>% of their base salary withheld to purchase shares quarterly, at a purchase price equal to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_003092" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardDiscountFromMarketPriceOfferingDate" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapEmployeeStockMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">85</ix:nonFraction>% of the fair market value of CIT common stock on the last business day of the quarterly offering period. The amount of common stock that may be purchased by a participant through the ESPP is generally limited to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_003093" name="cit:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardCeilingOnAmountOfPurchaseOfCommonStockUnderESPP" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapEmployeeStockMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">25,000</ix:nonFraction> per year. A total of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_003094" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardSharesPurchasedForAward" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapEmployeeStockMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">64,078</ix:nonFraction>, <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_003095" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardSharesPurchasedForAward" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapEmployeeStockMember_20180101_20181231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">61,722</ix:nonFraction> and <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_003096" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardSharesPurchasedForAward" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapEmployeeStockMember_20170101_20171231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">54,684</ix:nonFraction> shares were purchased under the plan in 2019, 2018 and 2017, respectively.</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Restricted Stock Units and Performance Stock Units</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">RSUs and PSUs are awarded at no cost to the recipient upon grant. RSUs are generally granted annually at the discretion of the Company, but may also be granted during the year to new hires. RSUs granted to employees and members of the Board during 2019 and 2018 generally were scheduled to vest either <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_003097_2"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_003098_2"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_003099_2">one third</span></span></span> per year for three years or <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_003100" name="cit:PercentageVestedAtEndOfVestingPeriod" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapRestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">100</ix:nonFraction>% after <ix:nonNumeric id="F_003101" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingPeriod1" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapRestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_20190101_20191231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">three years</ix:nonNumeric>. RSUs granted to employees were also subject to performance-based vesting based on a minimum Tier 1 Capital ratio. A limited number of vested stock awards are scheduled to remain subject to transfer restrictions through the first anniversary of the grant date for members of the Board who elected to receive stock in lieu of cash compensation for their retainer. Certain RSUs granted to directors, and in limited instances to employees, are designed to settle in cash and are accounted for as "liability" awards. The values of these cash-settled RSUs are re-measured at the end of each reporting period until the award is settled.</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Certain senior executives receive long-term incentive (&#8220;LTI&#8221;) awards, which are generally granted at the discretion of the Company annually.&#160;&#160;During 2019 and 2018, LTI has been awarded <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_003102" name="cit:LongTermIncentiveAwardPerformanceBasedRsuPercentage" contextRef="C_0001171825_20190101_20191231" decimals="2" scale="-2"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_003103" name="cit:LongTermIncentiveAwardPerformanceBasedRsuPercentage" contextRef="C_0001171825_20180101_20181231" decimals="2" scale="-2">50</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction>% in the form of PSUs based on after-tax ROTCE with a total shareholder return (&#8220;TSR&#8221;) adjustment factor (described more fully below), and <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_003104" name="cit:LongTermIncentiveAwardPerformanceStockUnitsPercentage" contextRef="C_0001171825_20190101_20191231" decimals="2" scale="-2"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_003105" name="cit:LongTermIncentiveAwardPerformanceStockUnitsPercentage" contextRef="C_0001171825_20180101_20181231" decimals="2" scale="-2">50</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction>% in the form of performance based RSUs (described above). </p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">PSUs awarded during 2019 and 2018 may be earned at the end of a <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_003106">three-year</span> performance period (2019 &#8211; 2021, and 2018 &#8211; 2020, respectively) based on after-tax ROTCE, which may be increased or decreased by up to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_003107" name="cit:SharebasedCompensationArrangementbySharebasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsAllowedAdjustmenttoROTCEforPerformanceBasedAward" contextRef="C_0001171825_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_citA2017And2018PerformanceSharesMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">20</ix:nonFraction>% depending on the Company&#8217;s 3-year cumulative TSR results relative to the component companies of the KBW Nasdaq Bank Index for the performance period. No increase is permitted if the Company&#8217;s TSR for the performance period is negative, and the overall payout for PSUs, including the TSR adjustment factor, may range from <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_003108" name="cit:PercentageVestedAtEndOfVestingPeriod" contextRef="C_0001171825_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_citA2017And2018PerformanceSharesMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">0</ix:nonFraction>% to a maximum of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_003109" name="cit:PercentageVestedAtEndOfVestingPeriod" contextRef="C_0001171825_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_citA2017And2018PerformanceSharesMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">150</ix:nonFraction>% of target. Performance measures for all PSU awards have a minimum threshold level of performance that must be achieved to trigger any payout&#59; if the threshold level of performance is not achieved, then no portion of the PSU target will be payable.</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The fair value of RSUs and PSUs that vested and settled in stock during 2019, 2018 and 2017 was $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_003110" name="cit:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsVestedAndSettledFairValue" contextRef="C_0001171825_20190101_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">51.1</ix:nonFraction> million, $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_003111" name="cit:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsVestedAndSettledFairValue" contextRef="C_0001171825_20180101_20181231" decimals="-5" scale="6">72.8</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_003112" name="cit:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsVestedAndSettledFairValue" contextRef="C_0001171825_20170101_20171231" decimals="-5" scale="6">59.0</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively. <span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;</span></p></ix:continuation>

<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Financing Commitments</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Commercial</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Financing commitments, referred to as loan commitments or lines of credit, primarily reflect CIT&#8217;s agreements to lend to its customers, subject to the customers&#8217; compliance with contractual obligations. At December 31, 2019, substantially all undrawn financing commitments were senior facilities. Most of the Company&#8217;s undrawn and available financing commitments are in the Commercial Banking segment.</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Financing commitments also include credit line agreements to Commercial Finance clients that are cancellable by us only after a notice period. The notice period is typically <ix:nonNumeric id="F_003189" name="cit:FinancingCommitmentsToTradeFinanceClientsThatAreCancelableOnlyAfterANoticePeriodTypicalNoticePeriod" contextRef="C_0001171825_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20190101_20191231" format="ixt-sec:durday">90</ix:nonNumeric> days or less. The amount available under these credit lines, net of the amount of receivables assigned to us, was $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_003190" name="cit:FinancingCommitmentsToTradeFinanceClientsThatAreCancelableOnlyAfterANoticePeriodAmount" contextRef="C_0001171825_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">172</ix:nonFraction> million&#160;&#160;and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_003191" name="cit:FinancingCommitmentsToTradeFinanceClientsThatAreCancelableOnlyAfterANoticePeriodAmount" contextRef="C_0001171825_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6">318</ix:nonFraction> million at December 31, 2019 and 2018<span style="font-style:italic;font-size:8pt;">, </span>respectively. </p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As financing commitments may not be fully drawn, may expire unused, may be reduced or canceled at the customer&#8217;s request, and may require the customer to be in compliance with certain conditions, total commitment amounts do not necessarily reflect actual future cash flow requirements.</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">150</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">CIT ANNUAL REPORT 2019</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000494_dcnt_1c1e0e0a-fafc-4eac-9833-d627a265dd0b">
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The table above excludes uncommitted revolving credit facilities extended by </span><span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Commercial Finance</span><span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> to its&#8217; clients for working capital purposes. In connection with these facilities, </span><span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Commercial Finance</span><span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> has the sole discretion throughout the duration of these facilities to determine the amount of credit that may be made available to its clients at any time and whether to honor any specific advance requests made by its clients under these credit facilities.</span></p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Letters of Credit</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In the normal course of meeting the needs of clients, CIT sometimes enters into agreements to provide financing and letters of credit. Standby letters of credit obligate the issuer of the letter of credit to pay the beneficiary if a client on whose behalf the letter of credit was issued does not meet its obligation. These financial instruments generate fees and involve, to varying degrees, elements of credit risk in excess of amounts recognized in the Consolidated Balance Sheets. To minimize potential credit risk, CIT generally requires collateral and in some cases additional forms of credit support from the client.</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Deferred Purchase Agreements</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">A Deferred Purchase Agreement (&#8220;DPA&#8221;) is provided in conjunction with factoring, whereby CIT provides a client with credit protection for trade receivables without purchasing the receivables. The trade receivable terms are generally <ix:nonNumeric id="F_003192" name="cit:DeferredPurchaseAgreementsCreditLineAgreementsCancellationNoticePeriod" contextRef="C_0001171825_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapPurchaseCommitmentExcludingLongtermCommitmentAxis_citDeferredPurchaseAgreementsMember_20190101_20191231" format="ixt-sec:durday">90</ix:nonNumeric> days or less. If the client&#8217;s customer is unable to pay an undisputed receivable solely as the result of credit risk, then CIT purchases the receivable from the client. The outstanding amount in the table above is the maximum potential exposure that CIT would be required to pay under all DPAs. This maximum amount would only occur if all receivables subject to DPAs default in the manner described above, thereby requiring CIT to purchase all such receivables from the DPA clients.</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The table above includes $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_003193" name="cit:DeferredPurchaseAgreementCreditProtectionAmountProvidedToClients" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapPurchaseCommitmentExcludingLongtermCommitmentAxis_citDeferredPurchaseAgreementsMember_20191231" decimals="-6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="6">1,966</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_003194" name="cit:DeferredPurchaseAgreementCreditProtectionAmountProvidedToClients" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapPurchaseCommitmentExcludingLongtermCommitmentAxis_citDeferredPurchaseAgreementsMember_20181231" decimals="-6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="6">1,895</ix:nonFraction> million of DPA credit protection at December 31, 2019 and 2018, respectively, related to receivables which have been presented to us for credit protection after shipment of goods has occurred and the customer has been invoiced. The table also includes $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_003195" name="cit:DeferredPurchaseAgreementsCreditLineAgreementsNetOfDeferredPurchaseAgreementCreditProtection" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapPurchaseCommitmentExcludingLongtermCommitmentAxis_citDeferredPurchaseAgreementsMember_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">94</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_003196" name="cit:DeferredPurchaseAgreementsCreditLineAgreementsNetOfDeferredPurchaseAgreementCreditProtection" contextRef="C_0001171825_us-gaapPurchaseCommitmentExcludingLongtermCommitmentAxis_citDeferredPurchaseAgreementsMember_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6">64</ix:nonFraction> million available under DPA credit line agreements, net of the amount of DPA credit protection provided at December 31, 2019 and 2018, respectively. The DPA credit line agreements specify a contractually committed amount of DPA credit protection and are cancellable by us only after a notice period. The notice period is typically 90 days or less.</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Purchase and Funding Commitments</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">CIT&#8217;s purchase commitments primarily relate to the Rail and Equipment Finance businesses.</p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000495" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyDisclosures" contextRef="C_0001171825_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000495_dcnt_809bc7e3-9040-404a-920e-b13a910ac9b3">
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Arial;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTE 22 &#8212; CONTINGENCIES</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000538" name="us-gaap:CommitmentsAndContingenciesPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001171825_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000538_dcnt_b03f221c-cba6-436c-a08e-3da9190216dc">
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Litigation and other Contingencies</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">CIT is involved, and from time to time in the future may be involved, in a number of pending and threatened judicial, regulatory, and arbitration proceedings as well as proceedings, investigations, examinations and other actions brought or considered by governmental and self-regulatory agencies. These matters arise in connection with the conduct of CIT&#8217;s business. At any given time, CIT may also be in the process of responding to subpoenas, requests for documents, data and testimony relating to such matters and engaging in discussions to resolve the matters (all of the foregoing collectively being referred to as &#8220;Litigation&#8221;). While most Litigation relates to individual claims, CIT is also subject to putative class action claims and similar broader claims and indemnification obligations. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In view of the inherent difficulty of predicting the outcome of Litigation matters and indemnification obligations, particularly when such matters are in their early stages or where the claimants seek indeterminate damages, CIT cannot state with confidence what the eventual outcome of the pending Litigation will be, what the timing of the ultimate resolution of these matters will be, or what the eventual loss, fines, or penalties related to each pending matter will be, if any. In accordance with applicable accounting guidance, CIT establishes reserves for Litigation when those matters present loss contingencies as to which it is both probable that a loss will occur and the amount of such loss can be reasonably estimated. Based on currently available information, CIT believes that the outcome of Litigation that is currently pending will not have a material adverse effect on the Company&#8217;s financial condition, but may be material to the Company&#8217;s operating results or cash flows for any particular period, depending in part on its operating results for that period. The actual results of resolving such matters may be substantially higher than the amounts reserved.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">For certain Litigation matters in which the Company is involved, the Company is able to estimate a range of reasonably possible losses in excess of established reserves and insurance. For other matters for which a loss is probable or reasonably possible, such an estimate cannot be determined. For Litigation and other matters where losses are reasonably possible, management currently estimates the aggregate range of reasonably possible losses as up to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_003197" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyRangeOfPossibleLossPortionNotAccrued" contextRef="C_0001171825_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">60</ix:nonFraction> million in excess of any established reserves and any insurance we reasonably believe we will collect related to those matters. This estimate represents reasonably possible losses (in excess of established reserves and insurance) over the life of such Litigation, which may span a currently indeterminable number of years, and is based on information currently available as of December 31, 2019. The Litigation matters underlying the estimated range will change from time to time, and actual results may vary significantly from this estimate.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Those Litigation matters for which an estimate is not reasonably possible or as to which a loss does not appear to be reasonably possible, based on current information, are not included within this estimated range and, therefore, this estimated range does not represent the Company&#8217;s maximum loss exposure.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:9pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The foregoing statements about CIT&#8217;s Litigation are based on the Company&#8217;s judgments, assumptions, and estimates and are </p></ix:nonNumeric></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">151</p>
<p style="text-align:right;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">CIT ANNUAL REPORT 2019</p>
